title: Bengaluru to Kalasa via Sakleshpur
blurb: Out of the city on NH75, past Hassan's temples, then into the Western Ghats: coffee estates around Sakleshpur and Mudigere and a long run of bends down into the Bhadra valley at Kalasa.
notes: Malnad roads are narrow and slippery in the monsoon (June to September), and forest stops have leeches.

title: Pollachi to Valparai
blurb: Flat coconut country to Aliyar dam, then forty numbered hairpins up the Anamalai hills, with Monkey Falls and Loam's View on the way and tea estates rolling over the top to Valparai.
notes: Elephants and lion-tailed macaques cross the ghat road; the Aliyar check post logs every vehicle.

title: Mysuru to Ooty via Gudalur
blurb: Through the Bandipur and Mudumalai forests, where elephants often stand by the road, then the long Naduvattam ghat from Gudalur up into the Nilgiris.
notes: The Bandipur and Mudumalai stretch is closed to traffic from 9 pm to 6 am.

title: Mangaluru to Chikkamagaluru via Charmadi Ghat
blurb: From the coast across the plains to Ujire, then the Charmadi ghat: a steep, forested climb of tight bends and waterfalls up to the coffee hills.
notes: Charmadi closes to heavy vehicles, and sometimes to all traffic, after monsoon landslides.

title: Udupi to Shivamogga via Agumbe
blurb: Temple town to the Agumbe ghat, a short climb of hairpins through rainforest to one of India's wettest villages and its sunset point, then down through the Malnad to Shivamogga.
notes: The ghat is narrow and closed to heavy vehicles in the monsoon.

title: Mumbai to Goa along the Konkan coast
blurb: The long way south: Konkan villages, sea forts, beaches and river crossings by Ratnagiri and Malvan before the road reaches Goa.
notes: Highway widening is still going on in places; the coastal stretches near Ratnagiri and Malvan are slower but quieter.

title: Pune to Kolad via Tamhini Ghat
blurb: A short monsoon favourite: past Mulshi lake and over Tamhini ghat, where the road runs under waterfalls, down to the Kundalika river at Kolad.
notes: At its best in the rains; go on a weekday to miss the crowds.

title: Mumbai to Malshej Ghat
blurb: Out past Kalyan and Murbad to the cliffs of Malshej, where the road climbs the Sahyadri wall between waterfalls and cloud.
notes: Landslides can close the ghat for days in heavy rain; check before you ride.

title: Chennai to Puducherry by the East Coast Road
blurb: The East Coast Road runs between the Bay of Bengal and backwaters, past the shore temples of Mamallapuram, to the French quarter of Puducherry.
notes: Ride early: the road fills with traffic by mid-morning at weekends.

title: Kochi to Munnar
blurb: From the backwaters through rubber and spice country to Adimali, then up into the tea gardens and waterfalls of the Kannan Devan hills.
notes: Mist cuts visibility on the ghat in the evenings, especially in the monsoon.

title: Madurai to Kodaikanal
blurb: Temple city to hill station: across the plains to Batlagundu, then the ghat climbs nearly two kilometres up the Palani hills through bends, viewpoints and pine forest.
notes: Use engine braking on the long way down.

title: Bengaluru to Madikeri
blurb: Past Mysuru to Kushalnagar's Tibetan settlement, then up into Kodagu: coffee, pepper and misty bends to Madikeri.
notes: The last climb to Madikeri is narrow; watch for buses on the bends.

title: Kolhapur to Goa via Amboli Ghat
blurb: Sugarcane country to the edge of the Sahyadris at Amboli, where the road drops past waterfalls in the fog to Sawantwadi and on to Goa.
notes: Amboli is at its best in the monsoon, with fog and waterfalls by the road.

title: Hyderabad to Srisailam
blurb: South through the Deccan to the Nallamala hills, then forest road through the Amrabad tiger reserve to the Krishna gorge and the temple town of Srisailam.
notes: The road through the tiger reserve is closed from 9 pm to 6 am.

title: Manali to Leh
blurb: The classic high-altitude ride: through the Atal Tunnel into Lahaul, past Keylong and Sarchu, and over the high passes of the Zanskar range down to Leh.
notes: Open roughly June to October. The passes are above 5,000 m: acclimatise a day at Keylong or Jispa, and carry fuel for the long stretch without pumps after Tandi. The elevation profile reads the hill above the Atal Tunnel, so it shows a bump there.

title: Shimla to Kaza through Kinnaur
blurb: Apple orchards at Narkanda, then the Sutlej gorge through Kinnaur on roads cut into cliffs, past Nako's lake into the cold desert of Spiti.
notes: Landslides are common around Malling and Nako, and the road beyond Reckong Peo is partly unpaved.

title: Jaipur to Jaisalmer
blurb: Across Rajasthan from the Pink City by Ajmer and the blue city of Jodhpur, the land drying into dunes before Jaisalmer's golden fort.
notes: Very hot from April to June; carry water, and fill up in Jodhpur and Pokaran.

title: Guwahati to Tawang via Sela Pass
blurb: Over the Brahmaputra plains to Tezpur, then up into Arunachal by Bomdila and Dirang and over Sela Pass at 4,170 m to the monastery town of Tawang.
notes: Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit for Arunachal Pradesh; Sela Pass can close with snow in winter.

title: Siliguri to Darjeeling
blurb: From the plains straight up the Himalayan foothills by Kurseong, sharing the bends with the toy train, to tea gardens and a view of Kanchenjunga.
notes: Hill Cart Road shares its bends with the toy train; Rohini Road is the quicker climb.

title: Rishikesh to Chopta
blurb: Up the Ganga by Devprayag and Rudraprayag, then the Mandakini valley to Ukhimath and the meadows of Chopta below Tungnath, the highest Shiva temple.
notes: Monsoon landslides often close the Badrinath highway; snow can block Chopta in winter. The road ends at Chopta, below the temple.

title: Bengaluru to Mullayanagiri
blurb: To Chikkamagaluru's coffee estates, then the narrow road up the Baba Budan range to Mullayanagiri, Karnataka's highest peak.
notes: The last stretch is single-lane; private vehicles may be stopped at weekends and on holidays.

title: Kozhikode to Wayanad via the Thamarassery Ghat
blurb: From the Malabar coast up the Thamarassery Ghat, nine hairpins from Adivaram to the Lakkidi viewpoint, onto the Wayanad plateau at Kalpetta.
notes: The ghat jams on weekend evenings, and heavy monsoon rain closes it now and then.

title: Leh to Nubra Valley over Khardung La
blurb: Up from Leh in loops to Khardung La at about 5,350 m, one of the highest roads riders can take, and down to the sand dunes and monastery of Diskit in the Nubra Valley.
notes: Nubra needs an Inner Line Permit. Spend two days in Leh first: the pass is over 5,300 m.

title: Leh to Pangong Tso over Chang La
blurb: East from Leh past Karu, over Chang La at about 5,360 m, through Tangtse and along the long blue lake of Pangong Tso to Spangmik.
notes: Pangong needs an Inner Line Permit. Streams can flood the road on summer afternoons; cross early.

title: Srinagar to Leh over Zoji La
blurb: From the Kashmir valley by Sonamarg over Zoji La, then through Drass and Kargil and over Namika La and Fotu La to Leh: the classic way into Ladakh.
notes: Zoji La opens from about May to November; near the top the road is broken and muddy, and it closes for snow.

title: Shillong to Sohra (Cherrapunji)
blurb: South from Shillong across the rolling Khasi Hills to Sohra on the edge of the plateau, among the wettest places on earth, with waterfalls and living root bridges below.
notes: In the monsoon the falls are at their biggest, but the road is wet and often in cloud.

title: Gangtok to Tsomgo Lake
blurb: A steep climb from Gangtok on the road towards Nathu La, from forest to bare mountainside, to the glacial Tsomgo Lake at about 3,750 m.
notes: A permit is needed, arranged through a registered operator in Gangtok; private vehicles from outside Sikkim may be turned back.

title: Kaza to Manali via Kunzum La
blurb: The second half of the Spiti circuit: Losar, the Kunzum La pass at about 4,500 m, the Chandratal turn-off and the long unpaved descent along the Chandra river to Manali.
notes: Closed by snow for most of the year; ask locally about water crossings and landslides between Kunzum La and Batal before you start.

title: Shimla to Chitkul via Sangla
blurb: Apple country at Narkanda, the Sutlej at Rampur, then up the Baspa valley through Sangla's orchards to Chitkul, the last village on the old road to Tibet.
notes: The Sangla to Chitkul road is narrow and often damaged by landslides; snow can close it from December to March.

title: Manali to Kasol via Kullu
blurb: Down the Beas valley past Kullu and Bhuntar, then up the Parvati valley to Kasol: deodar forest, riverside cafes and Manikaran's hot springs a little further on.
notes: The Parvati valley road is narrow with heavy tourist traffic in May, June and on weekends.

title: Dharamshala to Khajjiar
blurb: From the Dhauladhar foothills at Dharamshala through Chamba country to Dalhousie and the Khajjiar meadow ringed by deodars, with a small lake at its centre.
notes: Fog is common from July to September; fuel up in Dharamshala or Dalhousie.

title: Chandigarh to Shimla
blurb: The classic way up to Shimla: plains to Kalka, then the four-lane climb through Solan's pines to the old summer capital of British India.
notes: Weekend and holiday traffic is heavy beyond Solan; Shimla restricts vehicles on parts of the Mall.

title: Rishikesh to Badrinath
blurb: Up the Ganga and the Alaknanda through the five prayags and Joshimath to Badrinath, one of the four Char Dham shrines, with landslide gaps and mountain views the whole way.
notes: The road is cut by landslides each monsoon, and Badrinath's temple is shut from about November to April. Check road status before leaving Rishikesh.

title: Rishikesh to Sonprayag for Kedarnath
blurb: The Char Dham road up the Alaknanda to Rudraprayag, then along the Mandakini through Guptkashi to Sonprayag, where the walk to Kedarnath begins.
notes: Landslides block the Mandakini road often in the monsoon; Kedarnath itself is a walk or helicopter from Gaurikund, just beyond Sonprayag.

title: Kathgodam to Ranikhet via Nainital
blurb: From the railhead at Kathgodam up to Nainital's lake, over the ridge to Khairna on the Kosi river and on to Ranikhet's pine and oak slopes with Himalayan views.
notes: Nainital's lake road has a one-way system and parking is scarce in May and June.

title: Almora to Munsiyari
blurb: Across Kumaon through Thal to Munsiyari, a village facing the Panchachuli peaks, on a road that climbs and drops through oak forest and terraced fields.
notes: The last stretch past Thal is narrow with few fuel pumps; fill up in Almora or Bageshwar.

title: Dehradun to Mussoorie and Dhanaulti
blurb: A short climb from the Doon valley to Mussoorie's ridge, then on through deodar forest to Dhanaulti, a quiet clearing with views of the snow peaks on clear days.
notes: Weekend traffic into Mussoorie is heavy; start early and expect fog from July to September.

title: Srinagar to Sonamarg
blurb: Up the Sind valley from Srinagar through Ganderbal to Sonamarg, a wide meadow below glaciers, where the road to Zoji La begins.
notes: Sonamarg gets heavy snow from December to March; check that the road is open before leaving.

title: Srinagar to Pahalgam
blurb: South through Kashmir's saffron fields and apple orchards past Anantnag, then up the Lidder river to Pahalgam, a green valley ringed by pine-covered slopes.
notes: Saffron blooms in the Pampore fields in October and November.

title: Jammu to Srinagar via Banihal
blurb: The national highway from Jammu through Udhampur and Ramban, up the Chenab gorge and under the Pir Panjal at Banihal, then down into the Kashmir valley.
notes: Landslides and snow can close the highway for days; check traffic advisories before you start, and expect convoys on some stretches.

title: Leh to Hanle via Chumathang
blurb: Up the Indus to Upshi, then south through Chumathang's hot springs and Nyoma to Hanle, a remote village under one of the darkest skies in India, near its observatory.
notes: An Inner Line Permit is needed for this stretch and fuel is scarce beyond Upshi; carry spare fuel and plan for altitude of over 4,000 m.

title: Kargil to Padum via Pensi La
blurb: Up the Suru valley under the Nun Kun peaks to Rangdum's monastery, over Pensi La and down to Padum, the main town of Zanskar.
notes: Pensi La is shut by snow from about November to May; there is very little fuel or food between Kargil and Padum.

title: Madurai to Dhanushkodi via Rameswaram
blurb: Across the dry Ramanathapuram plain to the Pamban bridge, over the strait to Rameswaram's temple, then out along a thin spit of sand to the ruined town of Dhanushkodi at the island's tip.
notes: The road past Dhanushkodi is closed to vehicles after dark and winds are strong on the spit; check opening times locally.

title: Munnar to Thekkady via Kumily
blurb: From Munnar's tea slopes over the Western Ghats into Idukki's spice country, down to Kumily and Thekkady beside the Periyar reserve.
notes: Mist and heavy rain from June to August make the Ghat sections slippery; elephants sometimes cross near Periyar.

title: Bengaluru to Hampi
blurb: North on NH48 past Chitradurga's fort town to Hosapete, then the last few kilometres into Hampi's boulder-strewn ruins of the Vijayanagara capital.
notes: Summers are very hot; roadside food is limited between Chitradurga and Hosapete.

title: Hampi to Gokarna
blurb: From Hampi's ruins across the Deccan plateau to Hubballi, then down through the forests of the Western Ghats to Gokarna's temple town and its beaches.
notes: The Ghat section through the Uttara Kannada forests has sharp bends and few fuel pumps; fill up in Hubballi.

title: Gokarna to Udupi via Murudeshwar
blurb: The coast road south from Gokarna to Murudeshwar's seaside temple and its tall Shiva statue, then past river mouths and beaches to Udupi.
notes: NH66 is being widened in places, so expect diversions and dust; the monsoon from June to September brings heavy rain and rough seas.

title: Bengaluru to Kukke Subramanya via Shiradi Ghat
blurb: Past Hassan and Sakleshpur, then down the forested Shiradi Ghat to the Kumaradhara valley and the temple town of Kukke Subramanya.
notes: Shiradi Ghat has been closed or limited to light vehicles during monsoon repairs; check its status before leaving.

title: Shivamogga to Jog Falls
blurb: West from Shivamogga through the Sharavathi valley's forest and arecanut gardens to Jog Falls, where the river drops about 250 m in four streams.
notes: The falls are at their strongest after the monsoon and thin out by March.

title: Chikkamagaluru to Kudremukh via Kalasa
blurb: From Chikkamagaluru's coffee hills through Mudigere's estates to Kalasa, then along the Bhadra valley's forest road to Kudremukh and its grassy peak.
notes: Entering Kudremukh National Park needs a forest permit and leeches are common in the monsoon.

title: Coimbatore to Ooty via Coonoor
blurb: Across the plain to Mettupalayam, then the Coonoor ghat road with its hairpins through tea slopes, and on to Ooty's lake town.
notes: Weekend traffic on the Coonoor ghat is heavy, and monsoon rain can bring down trees and loose rock.

title: Bengaluru to Yercaud
blurb: South on NH44 through Hosur to Salem, then up the Shevaroy hills on a short, twisty climb to Yercaud's lake and coffee gardens.
notes: The climb to Yercaud is narrow, with buses and trucks; avoid riding them in heavy fog.

title: Visakhapatnam to Araku Valley
blurb: From the Visakhapatnam coast up through the Eastern Ghats' forest and ghat road, with viewpoints and tunnels along the way, to Araku's coffee plantations.
notes: Fog is common on the ghat in winter mornings; the monsoon from June to September can bring landslides.

title: Chennai to Tirupati
blurb: A fast run north across the coastal plain from Chennai into Andhra Pradesh, ending at Tirupati below the Tirumala hills and their famous temple.
notes: Heavy truck traffic on the national highway; Tirumala itself is a separate ghat road with its own timings for two-wheelers.

title: Thiruvananthapuram to Kanyakumari
blurb: South from Kerala's capital through coconut country and across the state border to Kanyakumari, where the Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal and Indian Ocean meet at India's southern tip.
notes: Kanyakumari is crowded at sunrise and sunset, especially on weekends and festivals.

title: Shravanabelagola to Belur: the Hoysala circuit
blurb: From the giant Jain statue at Shravanabelagola through Hassan to the Hoysala temples of Halebidu and Belur, finely carved in soapstone in the 12th century.
notes: The Shravanabelagola climb is barefoot on hot stone in the afternoon; temples close in the early evening.

title: Bengaluru to Nandi Hills
blurb: A short early-morning run north past Devanahalli to the Nandi Hills climb, with a steady ascent to the hilltop sunrise point above the plains.
notes: Gates open before dawn but fog is thick on winter mornings; weekends are very crowded.

title: Pune to Mahabaleshwar via Panchgani
blurb: Out of Pune over the Kath ghat to Wai, then up the Krishna valley to Panchgani's table land and on to Mahabaleshwar's strawberry farms and viewpoints.
notes: Weekends are crowded and the plateau is wrapped in fog during the monsoon; the road is closed to buses at some viewpoints.

title: Pune to Bhimashankar
blurb: North from Pune through Khed's farmland into the Sahyadri forest, climbing to Bhimashankar's temple and wildlife sanctuary at the head of the Bhima river.
notes: The last climb is narrow and slick in the monsoon; Giant squirrels live in the sanctuary and the temple queue is long on Mondays and festivals.

title: Mumbai to Nashik via Kasara Ghat
blurb: Up the Thane plain to the Kasara ghat, a climb into the Sahyadri with long views, then past Igatpuri's rock peaks and down to Nashik's river ghats and vineyards.
notes: Kasara ghat has heavy truck traffic and fog in the monsoon; fuel up before the climb.

title: Mumbai to Murud via Alibag
blurb: Down the Konkan coast through Alibag's beaches to Murud, where Janjira, a sea fort, stands on a rock just off the shore.
notes: Janjira Fort is reached by sail boat and closes during the monsoon from June to September.

title: Sambhajinagar to Ajanta via Ellora
blurb: Out of Aurangabad to Ellora's rock-cut temples, then across the Deccan plateau to the Ajanta caves, where Buddhist monasteries are cut into a horseshoe cliff.
notes: Ellora's caves are closed on Tuesdays and Ajanta's on Mondays; check opening days before you set out.

title: Panaji to Palolem
blurb: South from Panaji along Goa's coastal belt to Palolem's crescent beach, past churches, paddy fields and rivers.
notes: Holiday traffic builds up around Margao in December and January; the beach shacks close in the monsoon.

title: Panaji to Arambol
blurb: North through Mapusa's market town and the beach belt to Arambol, a quiet shore with a freshwater lake and cliffs at its far end.
notes: Roads are narrow with heavy scooter traffic in season; the beach shacks close in the monsoon.

title: Ahmedabad to Dhordo and the Rann of Kutch
blurb: Across Saurashtra's plain and over the Little Rann to Bhuj, then north on a straight road through the Banni grasslands to Dhordo, at the edge of the white salt desert.
notes: The salt flats are walkable only in winter; entry to the White Rann needs a permit available at Dhordo, and the Rann Utsav tent city runs from about November to February.

title: Rajkot to Sasan Gir
blurb: From Rajkot through Junagadh's old city to Sasan Gir, the home of the Asiatic lion, on flat Saurashtra roads with dry teak forest at the end.
notes: Gir National Park is closed from mid-June to mid-October and safari permits need booking ahead.

title: Dwarka to Somnath via Porbandar
blurb: Along Saurashtra's western coast from Dwarka's temple town to Porbandar, Gandhi's birthplace, and on to the seaside temple at Somnath.
notes: Wind and heat are strong on the open coast road; fuel and food stops are widely spaced.

title: Udaipur to Kumbhalgarh
blurb: From Udaipur's lakes through the Aravalli hills to Kumbhalgarh, a fort with a wall running for kilometres along the ridge.
notes: Hills are green after the monsoon and very dry by April; the fort wall walk can be hot at midday.

title: Udaipur to Mount Abu
blurb: South-west from Udaipur through Aravalli foothills to Abu Road, then the winding climb to Mount Abu, Rajasthan's only hill station.
notes: The climb from Abu Road has tight bends with trucks and buses; Mount Abu is crowded on weekends and in summer.

title: Jaipur to Pushkar via Ajmer
blurb: West on the Ajmer highway from Jaipur through Kishangarh, over the Nag Pahar hill by Ajmer, to Pushkar's sacred lake and its desert-edge camel fair ground.
notes: The Pushkar camel fair in November fills every room; the climb over Nag Pahar has heavy trucks.

title: Bhopal to Pachmarhi
blurb: South-east from Bhopal across the Narmada valley to Pipariya, then up the Satpura range to Pachmarhi, a hill town with caves, pools and a tiger reserve.
notes: Pachmarhi's lakes and caves are crowded on weekends; the jungle roads close during the monsoon in some years.

title: Jhansi to Khajuraho via Orchha
blurb: From Jhansi to Orchha's riverside palaces and temples, then across Bundelkhand to Khajuraho, where the famous temples carry carvings on every wall.
notes: Summers are fiercely hot; Khajuraho is quietest from October to March when the dance festival also runs in February.
